name: MSI MAG B650 Tomahawk WiFi
description: The MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi is the best AM5 board for most builds at $170 to $200: a strong VRM, Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE, three M.2 slots and BIOS Flashback.
quick: An ATX AM5 board on the B650 chipset with four DDR5 slots, a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot, three PCIe 4.0 M.2 slots, Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE and a Flash BIOS button. It sells for about $170 to $200.
bestFor: Ryzen 7000 and 9000 gaming builds that want solid power delivery and no missing basics
skipIf: you need PCIe 5.0 for a GPU or SSD, or USB4
verdict: The B650 Tomahawk WiFi is the AM5 board we would put in most builds. It gets the expensive parts right: power delivery that independent VRM roundups rate as comfortable even for 16-core Ryzen 9 chips, four DDR5 slots, three PCIe 4.0 M.2 slots, Wi-Fi 6E and 2.5 GbE. A Flash BIOS button on the rear panel means you can update the firmware for a new Ryzen chip without a CPU installed.

What you give up is PCIe 5.0 and USB4. The x16 slot runs at PCIe 4.0, which costs nothing measurable with an RTX 5070 or RX 9070 XT today; independent testing of current cards shows very small differences between PCIe 4.0 and 5.0 x16. The M.2 slots are also PCIe 4.0, which suits drives like the WD Black SN850X. If you want a 14,000 MB/s PCIe 5.0 SSD such as the Samsung 9100 Pro, look elsewhere.

Its closest rival is the [Gigabyte B650 Aorus Elite AX](/gear/gigabyte-b650-aorus-elite-ax/), which adds a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot for about $10 less but has a less generous feature set elsewhere. The step-up is the [MSI MAG X870 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-x870-tomahawk-wifi/) at $260 to $300, which adds PCIe 5.0 graphics and storage, USB4, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE. For a [Ryzen 7 9800X3D](/gear/ryzen-7-9800x3d/) gaming PC, the B650 Tomahawk is all the board you need, and the $80 saved buys a better GPU.
pros: Power delivery suits up to 16-core Ryzen 9
Flash BIOS button for CPU-less updates
cons: No PCIe 5.0 for GPU or M.2
No USB4
Older 2022 boxes need a BIOS update for Ryzen 9000

extra.heading: BIOS Updates
body: Boards made in 2022 and 2023 shipped with BIOS versions that support Ryzen 7000 only. Ryzen 9000 chips need a BIOS from mid-2024 or later, and the Ryzen 7 9800X3D and Ryzen 9 9950X3D need later versions still. Ryzen 8000G APUs need an early-2024 BIOS. If you are not sure what is installed, update before building; the Flash BIOS button works with no CPU, RAM or GPU installed.
Download the latest BIOS from MSI's support page for the MAG B650 Tomahawk WiFi, and use a USB stick of 32 GB or less formatted FAT32.
steps: Prepare the file
Extract the BIOS download and rename the file to MSI.ROM, then copy it to the root of the FAT32 USB stick.
Connect power
Connect the 24-pin and 8-pin CPU power cables, and switch the PSU on, but leave the PC off.
Use the Flash BIOS port
Plug the stick into the rear USB port marked Flash BIOS.
Press the button
Press the Flash BIOS button. Its LED flashes during the update.
Wait
When the LED stops flashing, after about five minutes, the update is done. Do not cut power during it.

faqs.q: Does the B650 Tomahawk WiFi support the Ryzen 7 9800X3D?
faqs.a: Yes, with a BIOS from late 2024 or later. Use the Flash BIOS button to update without a CPU if your board has an older version.

faqs.q: Does PCIe 4.0 bottleneck an RTX 5070 or RX 9070 XT?
faqs.a: No. Both cards use a full x16 link, and independent reviews show very small differences between PCIe 4.0 and 5.0 x16 with current GPUs.

faqs.q: Can the B650 Tomahawk handle a Ryzen 9 9950X3D?
faqs.a: Yes. Its power delivery is rated well for 16-core Ryzen 9 chips in independent VRM roundups. Update the BIOS first.

name: Gigabyte B650 Aorus Elite AX
description: The Gigabyte B650 Aorus Elite AX is a strong $160 to $190 AM5 board: one PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot, Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE and Q-Flash Plus for CPU-free BIOS updates.
quick: An ATX AM5 board on the B650 chipset with four DDR5 slots, a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot, one PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot, Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE and Q-Flash Plus. It sells for about $160 to $190.
bestFor: AM5 builders who want a PCIe 5.0 SSD slot without paying X870 prices
skipIf: you want PCIe 5.0 graphics, USB4 or the most M.2 slots
verdict: The B650 Aorus Elite AX is the cheapest way into a PCIe 5.0 SSD on a mainstream AM5 board from a major brand. One M.2 slot runs at PCIe 5.0 x4, so a drive like the Samsung 9100 Pro can run at its full rated 14,700 MB/s, while the graphics slot stays at PCIe 4.0 x16. Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE, four DDR5 slots and Q-Flash Plus round out a board that covers every gaming build.

The trade-off against the [MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-b650-tomahawk-wifi/) is mostly about where you want the spend. The Gigabyte gets the PCIe 5.0 SSD slot; the MSI is the stronger all-rounder in independent reviews, with three M.2 slots and a reputation for cool-running power delivery. For gaming, a PCIe 5.0 SSD makes little difference to load times, so the slot matters most if you move large files.

Gigabyte has also sold several versions under similar names, including the Elite AX V2 and the white Elite AX Ice. They differ in details like networking chips and M.2 layout, so check the exact model on the listing before comparing prices. The closest rival is the [ASUS TUF Gaming B650-Plus WiFi](/gear/asus-tuf-gaming-b650-plus-wifi/), which also has a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot but uses Wi-Fi 6. The step-up is the [MSI X870 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-x870-tomahawk-wifi/) for PCIe 5.0 graphics, USB4 and Wi-Fi 7.
pros: PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot at a B650 price
Q-Flash Plus for CPU-free BIOS updates
Solid power delivery for Ryzen 7 and 9
cons: PCIe 4.0 graphics slot
Several similar versions make listings confusing
Fewer extras than the B650 Tomahawk

Ryzen 8000G APUs need an early-2024 version. Q-Flash Plus updates the board with no CPU or memory installed.
Download the BIOS for your exact model and revision from Gigabyte's support page; the Elite AX, Elite AX V2 and Elite AX Ice use different files. Use a FAT32-formatted USB stick.

Wait for it to finish

faqs.q: Does the B650 Aorus Elite AX have PCIe 5.0?
faqs.a: Yes, for one M.2 SSD slot. The graphics slot is PCIe 4.0 x16, which does not hold back current GPUs in a measurable way.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Elite AX and Elite AX V2?
faqs.a: The V2 is a later revision with changes to details such as networking and M.2 layout. Check the exact model and use the matching BIOS file.

faqs.q: Can I update the B650 Aorus Elite AX BIOS without a CPU?
faqs.a: Yes. Q-Flash Plus flashes the BIOS from a USB stick with only the power supply connected.

name: ASUS TUF Gaming B650-Plus WiFi
description: The ASUS TUF Gaming B650-Plus WiFi is a durable $160 to $190 AM5 board with a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot, 2.5 GbE and BIOS FlashBack, though only Wi-Fi 6.
quick: An ATX AM5 board on the B650 chipset with four DDR5 slots, a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot, a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot, Wi-Fi 6, 2.5 GbE and BIOS FlashBack. It sells for about $160 to $190.
bestFor: AM5 builders who prefer ASUS's BIOS and want a PCIe 5.0 SSD slot on a budget
skipIf: you want Wi-Fi 6E or 7, or the best value at this price
verdict: The TUF Gaming B650-Plus WiFi is ASUS's value-focused AM5 board, and its pitch is the same as the Gigabyte Elite AX: a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot for a fast SSD, a PCIe 4.0 x16 graphics slot, 2.5 GbE and BIOS FlashBack. The TUF line leans on military-style styling and conservative component choices, and ASUS's BIOS is one of the easiest to navigate for first-time builders.

The weak spot is Wi-Fi. This board uses Wi-Fi 6, while the [MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-b650-tomahawk-wifi/) and [Gigabyte B650 Aorus Elite AX](/gear/gigabyte-b650-aorus-elite-ax/) both use Wi-Fi 6E at similar prices. That matters only if you have a 6 GHz router and a crowded wireless environment; with a wired connection or a Wi-Fi 6 router, it makes no difference. Power delivery is adequate for Ryzen 7 and fine for Ryzen 9 with decent case airflow, according to independent VRM roundups, though it is not the strongest in this group.

Choose it when it is the cheapest of the three on the day, or when you prefer ASUS's software and support. Otherwise the Tomahawk is the better all-rounder and the Elite AX the better spec sheet for the money. The step-up from ASUS is the TUF Gaming X870-Plus WiFi, or the [MSI X870 Tomahawk](/gear/msi-mag-x870-tomahawk-wifi/) for USB4 and Wi-Fi 7.
cons: Wi-Fi 6 rather than 6E at this price
Power delivery is solid but not class-leading
Rivals offer more for the same money

BIOS FlashBack works with only the power supply connected, so you can update before installing a new chip.

Download the BIOS from ASUS's support page for the TUF Gaming B650-Plus WiFi. The download includes a BIOSRenamer tool, which gives the file the exact name FlashBack expects. Use a FAT32-formatted USB stick.

Run BIOSRenamer in the extracted folder, then copy the renamed .CAP file to the root of the USB stick.
Connect power
Connect the 24-pin and 8-pin cables and turn on the PSU, leaving the PC off.
Insert the stick
Use the rear USB port marked BIOS FlashBack.
Hold the button
Press and hold the FlashBack button for about three seconds until the LED starts flashing.
Wait
The LED goes off when the update is complete. Do not unplug anything while it flashes.

faqs.q: Does the TUF Gaming B650-Plus WiFi have Wi-Fi 6E?
faqs.a: No. It uses Wi-Fi 6. The MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi and Gigabyte B650 Aorus Elite AX offer Wi-Fi 6E at similar prices.

faqs.q: Can the TUF B650-Plus run a Ryzen 9 9950X3D?
faqs.a: Yes, with an early-2025 or later BIOS and decent case airflow over the VRM. Update with BIOS FlashBack before installing the chip.

faqs.q: Does it support PCIe 5.0 SSDs?
faqs.a: Yes, in one M.2 slot. The other M.2 slots and the graphics slot run at PCIe 4.0.

name: MSI MAG X870 Tomahawk WiFi
description: The MSI X870 Tomahawk WiFi is the AM5 step-up at $260 to $300: PCIe 5.0 graphics and M.2, two 40 Gbps USB4 ports, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE on one ATX board.
quick: An ATX AM5 board on the X870 chipset with a PCIe 5.0 x16 slot, PCIe 5.0 M.2 storage, two USB4 ports at 40 Gbps, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE. It sells for about $260 to $300.
bestFor: high-end Ryzen 9000 builds that want PCIe 5.0, USB4 and the fastest networking
skipIf: you are building a gaming PC where a $180 B650 board does the same job
verdict: The X870 Tomahawk WiFi is the board to buy when you want every current AM5 feature without paying flagship prices. It has PCIe 5.0 for both the graphics card and an M.2 SSD, two USB4 ports at 40 Gbps, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE wired networking. Power delivery is built for 16-core Ryzen 9 chips, and MSI's tool-free M.2 and PCIe release latches make building easier.

The trade-off is cost against benefit. At $260 to $300 it costs about $80 to $100 more than the [B650 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-b650-tomahawk-wifi/), and for a gaming PC most of the extras do little. Current GPUs show tiny differences between PCIe 4.0 and 5.0 x16 in independent reviews, and a PCIe 5.0 SSD barely changes game load times. The value is real for creators moving large files to USB4 drives, for homes with multi-gig internet, and for anyone keeping the board through two or three CPU upgrades.

Its closest rival is the ASUS TUF Gaming X870-Plus WiFi at a similar price, and the Gigabyte X870 Aorus Elite WiFi7 is another strong option. Both are fine; the MSI stands out for its power delivery and practical build features. The cheaper way to get PCIe 5.0 graphics is a B850 board such as the [ASRock B850 Steel Legend WiFi](/gear/asrock-b850-steel-legend-wifi/), though you lose USB4. Pair this board with a [Ryzen 9 9950X3D](/gear/ryzen-9-9950x3d/) or a future AM5 chip, not a Ryzen 5.
pros: Flash BIOS button and tool-free latches
cons: About $80 to $100 more than a B650 Tomahawk
Extras add little for gaming alone
Early stock may need a BIOS update for newer X3D chips

Updating to the latest BIOS also brings memory compatibility and stability fixes, so it is worth doing on any new build.
MSI's Flash BIOS button updates the board without a CPU or memory. Download the BIOS for the MAG X870 Tomahawk WiFi from MSI's support page and use a FAT32 USB stick.

faqs.q: Is the X870 Tomahawk worth it over the B650 Tomahawk?
faqs.a: For gaming alone, usually not. The X870 adds PCIe 5.0 graphics, USB4, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE, which help creators and fast home networks more than frame rates.

faqs.q: Does the X870 Tomahawk support the Ryzen 7 9800X3D?
faqs.a: Yes. Early boards may need a BIOS update, which the Flash BIOS button can do without a CPU installed.

faqs.q: What is the difference between X870 and B850?
faqs.a: X870 requires USB4 and PCIe 5.0 graphics, while B850 makes PCIe 5.0 graphics optional and does not require USB4. Both use AM5 and DDR5.

name: ASRock B850 Steel Legend WiFi
description: The ASRock B850 Steel Legend WiFi is a smart $180 to $220 AM5 buy: a newer B850 board with PCIe 5.0 M.2, Wi-Fi, 2.5 GbE and Ryzen 9000 support from the box.
quick: An ATX AM5 board on the B850 chipset with four DDR5 slots, PCIe 5.0 M.2 storage, Wi-Fi, 2.5 GbE and BIOS Flashback. It launched in 2025 and sells for about $180 to $220.
bestFor: new Ryzen 9000 builds that want a 2025 board with PCIe 5.0 storage and no early-BIOS worries
skipIf: you can find a B650 Tomahawk on sale or need USB4
verdict: The B850 Steel Legend WiFi is the board for buyers who want something made for the current generation rather than a 2022 design with updates. B850 boards launched in early 2025 with BIOS versions that already support Ryzen 9000, so a [Ryzen 7 9800X3D](/gear/ryzen-7-9800x3d/) build is far less likely to need a flash before first boot. It brings a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot, Wi-Fi, 2.5 GbE, four DDR5 slots and the white-and-silver Steel Legend styling that suits light-themed builds.

The trade-off is that B850 is a small step over B650. The chipset is essentially the same, and the main difference is that B850 boards must offer PCIe 5.0 storage. Against the [MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-b650-tomahawk-wifi/), you gain PCIe 5.0 SSD support and newer firmware, and you usually pay $10 to $30 more. If you are not buying a PCIe 5.0 SSD, the Tomahawk on sale remains the better value.

Its closest rival is the MSI MAG B850 Tomahawk Max WiFi, a similar design at a similar price; the ASRock wins when it is cheaper on the day or when the white look matters. The step-up is the [MSI X870 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-x870-tomahawk-wifi/) for USB4, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE. For a new Ryzen 9000 build with a PCIe 5.0 SSD like the Samsung 9100 Pro, it is the simplest choice here: full-speed storage and a BIOS that already knows the CPU.
pros: Newer B850 board with Ryzen 9000 support out of the box
cons: Small upgrade over B650 for the extra cost

faqs.q: Is B850 better than B650?
faqs.a: Slightly. B850 boards must offer PCIe 5.0 storage and ship with newer BIOS versions, but the chipset is very similar. A discounted B650 board is often the better value.

faqs.q: Does the B850 Steel Legend need a BIOS update for Ryzen 9000?
faqs.a: Usually not for most Ryzen 9000 chips, since B850 boards shipped with support. Early units may need an update for the Ryzen 9 9950X3D.

faqs.q: Does the B850 Steel Legend have USB4?
faqs.a: No. USB4 is required on X870 boards, such as the MSI X870 Tomahawk WiFi, but not on B850.

name: MSI PRO B650M-A WiFi
description: The MSI PRO B650M-A WiFi is the best budget AM5 board at $130 to $160: micro-ATX, four DDR5 slots, two M.2 slots, Wi-Fi 6E and 2.5 GbE for gaming builds.
quick: A micro-ATX AM5 board on the B650 chipset with four DDR5 slots, a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot, two PCIe 4.0 M.2 slots, Wi-Fi 6E and 2.5 GbE. It sells for about $130 to $160.
bestFor: budget AM5 gaming builds with a Ryzen 5 or Ryzen 7 in a micro-ATX or ATX case
skipIf: you need more than two M.2 slots or plan a 16-core Ryzen 9
verdict: The PRO B650M-A WiFi is the board that makes budget AM5 builds work. For $130 to $160 you get Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE, four DDR5 slots and two PCIe 4.0 M.2 slots on a micro-ATX board that fits small and full-size cases. Pair it with a [Ryzen 5 7600](/gear/ryzen-5-7600/) or [Ryzen 5 9600X](/gear/ryzen-5-9600x/), 32 GB of DDR5-6000 and an RX 9060 XT, and nothing in the build feels compromised.

The compromises are in headroom. Two M.2 slots are enough for most gaming PCs, but storage hoarders will run out. The power delivery handles 65 W and 105 W class chips, including the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, according to independent reviews, but it is not the board for a 16-core Ryzen 9 under sustained heavy loads. The MSI PRO line also skips styling extras such as large heatsinks and RGB.

Its closest rival is the ASRock B650M Pro RS WiFi and similar micro-ATX boards at the same price; the MSI stands out for its Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE and Flash BIOS button. If you want an ATX board with three M.2 slots and stronger power delivery, the [MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-b650-tomahawk-wifi/) is the step-up for about $40 more. For a compact build, pair this board with the [Montech AIR 100 LITE](/gear/montech-air-100-lite/).
pros: Wi-Fi 6E and 2.5 GbE at a budget price
cons: Only two M.2 slots
Not ideal for 16-core Ryzen 9 chips
Plain styling and smaller heatsinks

faqs.q: Is the PRO B650M-A WiFi good for the Ryzen 7 9800X3D?
faqs.a: Yes. Its power delivery handles the 120 W 9800X3D, according to independent reviews. Update to a late-2024 or newer BIOS first.

faqs.q: Does the PRO B650M-A WiFi fit in an ATX case?
faqs.a: Yes. Micro-ATX boards fit in any ATX case, using a subset of the mounting holes.

faqs.q: How many M.2 slots does the PRO B650M-A WiFi have?

name: MSI MAG B550 Tomahawk
description: The MSI B550 Tomahawk is the best-value AM4 board at $140 to $180: strong power delivery, PCIe 4.0, 2.5 GbE plus 1 GbE and BIOS Flashback+, but no Wi-Fi.
quick: An ATX AM4 board on the B550 chipset with four DDR4 slots, a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot, one PCIe 4.0 and one PCIe 3.0 M.2 slot, 2.5 GbE plus 1 GbE and BIOS Flashback+. There is no Wi-Fi, and it sells for about $140 to $180.
bestFor: AM4 builds and upgrades with Ryzen 3000 or 5000, including 16-core chips
skipIf: you need built-in Wi-Fi or are starting a new build that could go AM5
verdict: The B550 Tomahawk became the default AM4 board in 2020 for one reason: power delivery that independent VRM roundups rated among the coolest-running in its class, strong enough for a 16-core Ryzen 9 3950X or 5950X. Add a PCIe 4.0 x16 slot, one PCIe 4.0 M.2 slot, dual Ethernet at 2.5 GbE and 1 GbE, and BIOS Flashback+, and it still makes sense in 2026 for anyone staying on AM4.

The main gap is wireless. There is no Wi-Fi, so budget about $20 to $40 for a PCIe or USB adapter if you cannot run a cable. The second M.2 slot runs at PCIe 3.0 through the chipset, which is fine for a game library drive. And B550 does not support Ryzen 2000 or Ryzen 3000G APUs, so check your CPU before buying.

The bigger question is whether to buy AM4 at all. A [Ryzen 7 5700X3D](/gear/ryzen-7-5700x3d/) on this board is a strong gaming upgrade for an existing DDR4 system. For a brand-new build, an AM5 board like the [MSI PRO B650M-A WiFi](/gear/msi-pro-b650m-a-wifi/) costs about the same and has a future CPU path. Among AM4 boards, its closest rival is the [Gigabyte X570S Aorus Elite AX](/gear/gigabyte-x570s-aorus-elite-ax/), which adds Wi-Fi 6 and more PCIe 4.0 lanes for about $50 more. The step-up for a 16-core build is the [ASUS ROG Strix X570-E](/gear/asus-rog-strix-x570-e-gaming/), though stock is thin.
pros: Power delivery strong enough for 16-core Ryzen 9
cons: No Wi-Fi
Second M.2 slot is PCIe 3.0
No support for Ryzen 2000 or 3000G APUs

Download the latest BIOS for the MAG B550 Tomahawk from MSI's support page. Use a FAT32 USB stick, ideally 32 GB or smaller, since some older boards reject large drives.

faqs.a: Yes. Its power delivery is rated well for 16-core Ryzen 9 chips in independent VRM roundups.

faqs.q: Does the B550 Tomahawk support the Ryzen 7 5700X3D?
faqs.a: Yes, with a recent BIOS. Use BIOS Flashback+ to update without a CPU if your board has older firmware.

faqs.q: Does the B550 Tomahawk have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: No. Use Ethernet or add a PCIe or USB Wi-Fi adapter for about $20 to $40.

faqs.q: Should I buy AM4 or AM5 in 2026?
faqs.a: Buy AM4 only to upgrade an existing DDR4 system. For a new build, AM5 boards cost about the same and support future Ryzen chips.

bestFor: 16-core Ryzen 9 3950X or 5950X builds that want the strongest AM4 platform
skipIf: you are not running a Ryzen 9, or could put the money toward an AM5 build
verdict: The Strix X570-E Gaming WiFi II is the AM4 board for a 16-core Ryzen 9 that will be worked hard. ASUS built it with power delivery that independent VRM roundups placed near the top of the X570 range, along with two PCIe 4.0 M.2 slots, Wi-Fi 6E, 2.5 GbE and BIOS FlashBack. For a Ryzen 9 3950X rendering or compiling for hours, it keeps the VRM cool with headroom to spare.

The problem is price. At $300 to $350 with limited stock, it costs more than an MSI X870 Tomahawk, a newer AM5 board with PCIe 5.0 and USB4. The X570 chipset also uses a small fan, which some owners notice at idle, though it is quiet on most units. Those costs make sense only if you already own a Ryzen 9 and DDR4 and want the best home for them.

Its closest rival is the [Gigabyte X570S Aorus Elite AX](/gear/gigabyte-x570s-aorus-elite-ax/), which has a fanless chipset, strong power delivery and Wi-Fi 6 for about $100 less; for most 16-core builds, it is the better value. The [MSI B550 Tomahawk](/gear/msi-mag-b550-tomahawk/) also handles a 3950X for less than half the price. If you are starting fresh, an AM5 board and a Ryzen 9000 chip is the stronger long-term buy than paying a premium for AM4 in 2026.
pros: Top-tier AM4 power delivery for 16-core chips
cons: Costs more than newer AM5 boards
Chipset fan
Stock is limited in 2026

extra.heading: BIOS Updates
body: The WiFi II version launched in 2021 with Ryzen 5000 support. The Ryzen 7 5700X3D, released in early 2024, needs a newer BIOS, and later versions also improve memory compatibility. X570 boards support Ryzen 2000, 3000 and 5000 desktop chips, but check ASUS's CPU support list for your exact model and BIOS version.

BIOS FlashBack updates the board with only the power supply connected. Download the BIOS for the ROG Strix X570-E Gaming WiFi II from ASUS's support page, not the original X570-E, since the files differ.
steps: Rename with BIOSRenamer
Run the BIOSRenamer tool included in the download, then copy the renamed .CAP file to the root of a FAT32 USB stick.
Connect power
Connect the 24-pin and 8-pin cables and switch on the PSU, with the PC off.
Insert the stick
Use the rear USB port labeled BIOS FlashBack.
Hold the button
Press and hold the FlashBack button for about three seconds until the LED flashes.
Wait for the LED to stop
When it goes out, the update is complete.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Strix X570-E and the X570-E WiFi II?
faqs.a: The WiFi II is a 2021 refresh that upgrades wireless to Wi-Fi 6E. Use the BIOS file for your exact version.

faqs.q: Is the Strix X570-E worth it for a Ryzen 9 3950X?
faqs.a: Only if you want the strongest AM4 power delivery. The Gigabyte X570S Aorus Elite AX and MSI B550 Tomahawk handle a 3950X for much less.

faqs.q: Is the X570 chipset fan loud?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most owners report it is quiet, though some notice it at idle in a silent room.

name: Gigabyte X570S Aorus Elite AX
description: The Gigabyte X570S Aorus Elite AX is the best AM4 board for a 16-core Ryzen at $190 to $230: fanless chipset, PCIe 4.0, Wi-Fi 6, 2.5 GbE and Q-Flash Plus.
quick: An ATX AM4 board on the fanless X570S chipset with PCIe 4.0 graphics and storage, Wi-Fi 6, 2.5 GbE and Q-Flash Plus. It sells for about $190 to $230.
bestFor: AM4 builds with a Ryzen 9 3950X or 5950X that want Wi-Fi and a silent chipset
skipIf: you are starting a new build where AM5 makes more sense
verdict: The X570S Aorus Elite AX is the AM4 board to buy for a 16-core Ryzen when you want Wi-Fi and do not want to pay ROG prices. The X570S chipset is a revision of X570 that runs without a fan, so there is no small whine at idle. Power delivery is well suited to a Ryzen 9 3950X or 5950X according to independent VRM roundups, and you get PCIe 4.0 for graphics and storage, Wi-Fi 6, 2.5 GbE and Q-Flash Plus.

The trade-off against the [MSI B550 Tomahawk](/gear/msi-mag-b550-tomahawk/) is about $50 more for Wi-Fi 6 and more PCIe 4.0 lanes through the chipset. If you run several fast NVMe drives or need wireless, that is worth paying. If you use Ethernet and one or two SSDs, the B550 Tomahawk does the same job for less.

Its closest rival in the X570 class is the [ASUS ROG Strix X570-E Gaming WiFi II](/gear/asus-rog-strix-x570-e-gaming/), which has stronger power delivery and Wi-Fi 6E but costs about $100 more and keeps the chipset fan. The cheaper X570 alternative, the [ASUS TUF Gaming X570-Plus](/gear/asus-tuf-gaming-x570-plus-wifi/), has a fan and only 1 GbE. For a new build in 2026, an AM5 board like the [MSI B650 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-b650-tomahawk-wifi/) costs about the same and has a future upgrade path; buy this board to finish or upgrade an AM4 system you already own.
cons: About $50 more than a B550 Tomahawk
Wi-Fi 6 rather than 6E
AM4 is a dead-end platform

extra.heading: BIOS Updates
body: X570S boards launched in 2021 with Ryzen 3000 and 5000 support. The Ryzen 7 5700X3D needs a BIOS from 2024 or later, and newer versions improve memory support and stability. Check Gigabyte's CPU support list for your board revision before buying an older chip.

Q-Flash Plus updates the board with only the power supply connected, so you can flash before installing a new CPU. Download the BIOS for the X570S Aorus Elite AX and your board revision from Gigabyte's support page.
steps: Rename the file
Rename the extracted BIOS file to GIGABYTE.bin and copy it to the root of a FAT32 USB stick.
Connect power
Connect the 24-pin and 8-pin cables and switch on the PSU, with the PC off.
Insert the stick
Use the rear USB port labeled for Q-Flash Plus.
Press Q-Flash Plus

Wait
The board may restart during the process. When the LED stops, it is done.

faqs.q: What is the difference between X570 and X570S?
faqs.a: X570S is a revised X570 chipset that runs without a fan. Features and CPU support are otherwise very similar.

faqs.q: Is the X570S Aorus Elite AX good for a Ryzen 9 3950X?
faqs.a: Yes. Its power delivery suits 16-core Ryzen 9 chips, and it adds Wi-Fi 6 and a fanless chipset for about $100 less than the Strix X570-E.

faqs.q: Does the X570S Aorus Elite AX support the Ryzen 7 5700X3D?
faqs.a: Yes, with a 2024 or later BIOS. Use Q-Flash Plus to update without a CPU.

name: ASUS TUF Gaming X570-Plus (Wi-Fi)
description: The ASUS TUF Gaming X570-Plus (Wi-Fi) is an aging $160 to $190 AM4 board: two PCIe 4.0 M.2 slots and Wi-Fi, but only 1 GbE and a chipset fan for the money.
quick: An ATX AM4 board on the X570 chipset with two M.2 slots, built-in Wi-Fi, 1 GbE and a chipset fan. It launched in 2019 and sells for about $160 to $190.
bestFor: AM4 owners who find it discounted and want PCIe 4.0 with built-in Wi-Fi
skipIf: you can get a B550 Tomahawk or X570S Aorus Elite AX for similar money
verdict: The TUF Gaming X570-Plus (Wi-Fi) was a sensible budget X570 board in 2019. It brought PCIe 4.0 for graphics and two M.2 slots, built-in Wi-Fi and ASUS's TUF component choices to a price well below the ROG boards. In 2026, though, it sits at $160 to $190 and is outclassed by boards from the same AM4 era.

The weak points are networking and value. It has 1 GbE rather than 2.5 GbE, and its Wi-Fi is a generation behind the Wi-Fi 6 and 6E of later boards. The X570 chipset uses a small fan. Power delivery is the lightest of the X570 boards here: independent VRM roundups found it fine for 8- and 12-core chips, while a 16-core Ryzen 9 3950X wants good case airflow over the heatsinks.

Its closest rival is the [MSI B550 Tomahawk](/gear/msi-mag-b550-tomahawk/), which costs about the same, has stronger power delivery and 2.5 GbE, though no Wi-Fi. For about $30 more, the [Gigabyte X570S Aorus Elite AX](/gear/gigabyte-x570s-aorus-elite-ax/) adds Wi-Fi 6, 2.5 GbE and a fanless chipset, and it is the board to step up to. Buy the TUF X570-Plus only below $140, or to replace a failed board of the same model without reinstalling Windows.
pros: PCIe 4.0 graphics and two M.2 slots
Broad AM4 CPU support with BIOS updates
cons: Only 1 GbE
Lightest power delivery of the X570 boards here
Chipset fan
Poor value against the B550 Tomahawk and X570S Elite AX

extra.heading: BIOS Updates
body: This board launched in 2019 for Ryzen 3000. Ryzen 5000 chips need a BIOS from late 2020 or later, and the Ryzen 7 5700X3D needs a 2024-era BIOS. Old stock may ship with firmware that predates both, so check the BIOS version before installing a newer CPU.

Check the rear I/O and the manual for your board revision for a BIOS FlashBack button. If yours has one, it updates the board without a CPU, using a renamed file from ASUS's BIOSRenamer tool. If not, install a CPU the current BIOS supports, such as a Ryzen 3000 chip, and update with EZ Flash 3 from inside the BIOS before swapping in the new processor.
steps: Download the right file
Get the latest BIOS for the TUF Gaming X570-Plus (Wi-Fi) from ASUS's support page and copy it to a FAT32 USB stick.
Boot with a supported CPU
If there is no FlashBack button, boot with a CPU the installed BIOS supports.
Open EZ Flash 3
Enter the BIOS, switch to Advanced Mode and open the EZ Flash 3 utility under Tool.
Select the file
Choose the BIOS file on the USB stick and confirm. Do not power off during the update.
Install the new CPU
Shut down, swap in the newer Ryzen chip and load optimized defaults.

faqs.q: Does the TUF Gaming X570-Plus support Ryzen 5000?
faqs.a: Yes, with a BIOS from late 2020 or later. The Ryzen 7 5700X3D needs a newer 2024-era BIOS.

faqs.q: Is the TUF X570-Plus good for a Ryzen 9 3950X?
faqs.a: It works, but it is not the best choice. Its power delivery is the lightest of the X570 boards here, so a 3950X needs good case airflow.

faqs.q: TUF X570-Plus or B550 Tomahawk?
faqs.a: The B550 Tomahawk is the better board for most builds, with stronger power delivery and 2.5 GbE. The TUF X570-Plus wins only on built-in Wi-Fi.

name: MSI MAG B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi
amazon: MSI MAG B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi motherboard
description: The MSI B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi is the AM5 board to beat around $230: 80 A power stages, PCIe 5.0 for the GPU and an M.2 SSD, Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE networking.
quick: The MAG B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi is an ATX AM5 board with 80 A smart power stages, a PCIe 5.0 x16 slot and a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot. It adds Wi-Fi 7, 5 GbE and MSI's Flash BIOS button.
bestFor: Ryzen 7000 and 9000 gaming builds, including a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, that want current connectivity without X870 prices
skipIf: you need USB4 ports, or a $170 B650 board already covers what you use
verdict: The MSI MAG B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi takes the formula that made the [B650 Tomahawk](/gear/msi-mag-b650-tomahawk-wifi/) the default AM5 board and brings it up to date. MSI lists 80 A smart power stages, which is more than enough for a Ryzen 7 9800X3D or a 16-core Ryzen 9 at stock or with PBO. The graphics slot and one M.2 slot run at PCIe 5.0, and networking steps up to Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE.

Be honest about how much of that you will use. Independent reviews show current graphics cards, including the RTX 5090, losing only a percent or two on PCIe 4.0 x16, so the Gen5 slot is future-proofing rather than a speed boost today. A PCIe 5.0 SSD such as the [Samsung 9100 Pro](/gear/samsung-9100-pro/) loads games about as fast as a good Gen4 drive. What you will notice is the faster networking and the Flash BIOS button, which updates the board from a USB stick without a CPU or memory installed.

At $210 to $250 it costs $30 to $60 more than the B650 Tomahawk and sits close to the [ASRock B850 Steel Legend WiFi](/gear/asrock-b850-steel-legend-wifi/), which is often a little cheaper with 2.5 GbE instead of 5 GbE. The [MSI X870 Tomahawk WiFi](/gear/msi-mag-x870-tomahawk-wifi/) adds USB4 for another $40 to $60. For most AM5 gaming builds, the B850 Tomahawk MAX is the sweet spot. MSI also lists V1 and II revisions; check the exact name on the listing.
pros: 80 A power stages handle any AM5 chip
Strong value for the feature set
cons: No USB4, unlike X870 boards
Costs $30 to $60 more than a B650 Tomahawk
Gen5 slots add little speed with today's parts

extra.heading: BIOS Updates
body: Update the BIOS before you install Windows, especially with a Ryzen 9000 chip. Newer AGESA releases improve memory compatibility and boost behavior, and the first boot with DDR5 memory training can take a minute or two, which is normal.
The Flash BIOS button lets you update without a CPU or memory installed.
steps: Download the BIOS
Get the latest BIOS for the MAG B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi from MSI's support page, matching the exact board name and revision.
Prepare a USB stick
Format a USB drive as FAT32, extract the file and rename it as MSI's instructions specify for this board.
Use the Flash BIOS port
Plug the stick into the rear USB port marked Flash BIOS, connect the 24-pin and CPU power cables, and press the Flash BIOS button.
Wait for the light
The LED flashes during the update. When it stops, the update is done; do not cut power while it flashes.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi and B650 Tomahawk WiFi?
faqs.a: PCIe 5.0 and networking. The B850 board has a PCIe 5.0 graphics slot and PCIe 5.0 M.2, plus Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE, against PCIe 4.0, Wi-Fi 6E and 2.5 GbE on the B650 board.

faqs.q: Can the B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi run a Ryzen 7 9800X3D?
faqs.a: Yes. Its 80 A power stages are more than enough for the 9800X3D at stock or with PBO. Update to a current BIOS first.

faqs.q: Is the B850 Tomahawk MAX WiFi worth it over X870?
faqs.a: For most gaming builds, yes. X870 boards like the X870 Tomahawk add USB4 for about $40 to $60 more; if you do not use USB4 devices, the B850 board gives up nothing else that matters.
